name: ux-craft
description: Book-grounded UX engine for implementing, mocking, and reviewing web and mobile UIs, layouts, and user flows, plus marketing and transactional emails. Operationalizes the UX canon — Krug (self-evidence, trunk test), Norman (affordances/signifiers/feedback), Garrett's five planes, Cooper's goal-directed design, Nielsen's heuristics, Wroblewski's mobile-first, Yablonski's Laws of UX, Weinschenk's behavioral science, Fogg/Cialdini/Eyal persuasion with a hard ethics gate, Tidwell patterns, Lidwell principles, Refactoring UI hierarchy tactics, Lean UX mock-to-learn — as three modes (Build / Review / Advise) over eight references: psychology-laws (research-cited mechanisms), review-playbook (multi-lens pass with severity honesty, intentional-vs-accidental deviation handling, evidence-format findings with pasteable fixes, and prompt-injection guards for reviewed content), flows-and-forms (GDS one-thing-per-page, validation timing, state machines, undo vs confirmation, wayfinding), mobile-ux (touch targets, thumb zones, iOS/Material platform grammar, RN notes), email-ux (two-second triage contract, client rendering constraints, transactional patterns, CAN-SPAM/GDPR compliance floor), ux-writing (microcopy patterns, tone matrix, Butterick typography), ai-product-ux (AI inputs/wayfinding/governors/narration/trust/tuners with friction-to-risk calibration and prompt-injection-aware retrieval rules), and per-surface pre-ship checklists incl. WCAG 2.2 quick pass and an AI-feature gate. The UX brain to design-craft's visual hands: it owns whether the thing works for humans; design-craft owns whether it looks intentional. v1.1.1 adds two pre-ship checklist floors routinely forgotten in mocks: designed not-found/error routes (no dead ends) and legally required links (privacy/terms/cookie consent). v1.2 adds a Working-posture section recalibrated for current-model behaviour (Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 prompting guidance): reviews run as two passes that must never be merged — find wide (every finding, including uncertain and low-severity ones) then filter hard (rank, merge, drop) — because a reviewer asked to be conservative reports less rather than better, and severity calibration is a filter-pass job; reports stay proportional to their findings rather than to the template, with empty sections dropped and no closing restatement; scope is held (review what was pointed at, raise a deeper problem in a sentence instead of auditing it uninvited); lens fan-out becomes the exception for scopes that genuinely exceed one pass, briefed content-first and questions-last, never spawned to grade its own findings, with the post-fix re-check scoped to regression on what changed; corrections are narrated only when they change the user's decisions; and every capture taken during a review must be opened, since a rendered screenshot nobody read is not evidence. ai-product-ux gains a Narration section treating the assistant's own words as a designed surface — progress-update shape, outcome-first closing turns, a threshold for narrating self-corrections, a caveat budget, voice specified by positive samples rather than prohibitions, and the verbose-is-not-transparent separation of trace depth from prose length — plus a narration-cadence line in the AI-feature pre-ship checklist and the matching question in the AI review lens.
